title: Testosterone
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows your level of testosterone. Both men and women have this hormone.
why: In men, for low sex drive, tiredness, or trouble conceiving. In women, for irregular periods, acne, or extra hair growth.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take hormones or sports supplements
If you take birth control pills
Your cycle day, if you are a woman
If you work nights or sleep poorly

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Usually in the morning, before about 11 a.m. Women will be told the cycle day by their doctor.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when
Sometimes the doctor asks you to repeat the test. The level changes from day to day

faq.q: Why is testosterone tested in the morning?
faq.a: It is highest in the morning. Normal ranges are set for a morning test.

faq.q: Do women need a testosterone test?
faq.a: Yes, if your doctor ordered it. Women have it too, just in smaller amounts.

reminders.text: Testosterone test tomorrow morning. Do not eat after dinner, get a good sleep, and skip workouts.
